claims.title: Saturn v5.7.1 is a technically defensible production candidate
claims.statement: The v5.7.1 dual-head U-Net-primary pipeline, calibrated measurement path, morphology-neutral global tracking, and biologist-facing reporting operate consistently across GUI, batch, tuner, and study workflows without using WT morphology as a technical acceptance target.
claims.biological_meaning: Technical-valid nuclei and tracks remain measurable across plausible WT and mutant morphology, with provenance sufficient for specimen-level comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration is resolved before physical thresholds and measurements
Dual-head checkpoint identity and SHA-256 are enforced
Morphology warnings do not become comparative technical vetoes
Tracking has no duplicate Z observations and rejects impossible joins without deleting source detections
Primary reports agree with source tables and use specimen-level biological terminology
All supported execution entry points use the same production semantics
Automated and adversarial validation covers measurement, tracking, reporting, and failure paths
known_limitations: Below-2-um reconstructed tracks can include genuine short nuclei, optical tips, split fragments, or noise; their specimen-level influence is reported automatically without excluding them from the primary population
Body width is apparent mask width, not PSF-corrected physical chromatin width
Existing repeated 2D ROIs cannot establish anatomical SV volume
non_claims: The pipeline does not establish a biological KJ-versus-WT effect from one pilot specimen per group
The pipeline does not currently measure anatomical SV volume from a 3D organ mask

claims.title: Manual corrections are replayable and preserve original evidence
claims.statement: GUI corrections operate on authoritative filled instance masks or explicit cross-slice constraints, are stored append-only, and deterministically regenerate measurements, tracking, overlays, and reports without overwriting the original run.
claims.biological_meaning: A reviewer can correct a technical segmentation or tracking error without converting unusual WT or mutant morphology into an exclusion rule or losing the original model result.
acceptance_criteria: Original masks, measurements, tracks, and reports are never overwritten
Every correction records stable instance identity, reviewer, timestamp, reason, before and after hashes, software version, profile, checkpoint, and calibration provenance
2D edits operate on filled instance masks and trigger deterministic remeasurement and full-specimen retracking
Track constraints cannot create duplicate source instances, same-Z collisions, cross-specimen links, or missing track IDs
Morphology alone cannot justify technical exclusion or prevent a link
GUI, batch, study, and regenerated reports identify the applied correction revision
known_limitations: The initial implementation may expose only a subset of the versioned correction actions
A correction revision is non-production until the audit gate passes
non_claims: Manual correction does not establish that every retained object is biologically normal
Correction frequency is not a biological phenotype

claims.title: Subpixel central-body chord width replaces quantized EDT width
claims.statement: Apparent nucleus body width is measured by perpendicular boundary-to-boundary chords through the central filled-mask body and is used as the primary width field.
claims.biological_meaning: A rotation-stable apparent width of the segmented central nucleus body, excluding tapered endpoints.
claims.population: technically valid U-Net instances with sufficient centerline chord samples
acceptance_criteria: Known-width synthetic masks are recovered within stated tolerance
Rotation does not create material width bias
One-pixel erosion and dilation sensitivity is quantified as technical QC
Too few valid chords produce unavailable rather than fabricated width
Largest-area valid Z plane supplies representative track width
Reported length/body-width ratio pairs length and width from the same representative Z plane
Legacy EDT fields remain explicitly labelled and do not drive primary reports
known_limitations: Affected by segmentation boundary, focus, annotation thickness, and lateral PSF
An over-thick learned foreground mask can overestimate apparent width because every chord terminates at that mask boundary
Not an optical deconvolution or PSF-corrected chromatin diameter
non_claims: Does not establish true molecular-scale nucleus width

claims.title: Raw-signal FWHM replaces mask-boundary width as the comparative width
claims.statement: Comparative nucleus width is the background-corrected full width at half maximum of the raw intensity profile sampled perpendicular to the centerline and restricted to the object's own instance mask. It replaces the filled-mask contour chord as the width presented in biological reports; the chord and the distance-transform width remain explicitly named technical diagnostics.
claims.biological_meaning: An apparent optical signal width that supports comparison between experimental groups. It is not an absolute nucleus diameter.
claims.population: technically valid instances whose profile shows a half-maximum crossing on both sides while still inside the instance mask
calibration_dependencies: numerical aperture and emission wavelength when PSF correction is explicitly enabled
source_dependencies: instance mask used only to scope the profile, never to set the width
acceptance_criteria: Known-width synthetic profiles are recovered monotonically and the measured value is reported with its compression in the sub-resolution regime stated
Width is independent of segmentation mask thickness: inflating the mask must not change the reported width
Signal outside the object's own instance mask must not set the half maximum, the crossing, or the integrated signal
A profile without a half-maximum crossing on both sides inside the mask is unavailable rather than inflated
No morphological dilation appears anywhere in the measurement path, including background estimation
Rotation does not create material width bias
Representative width and the paired centerline length come from the same observed Z plane
Integrated profile signal is reported only as technical QC and never as a biological endpoint or acceptance gate
The comparative-only interpretation travels with the value in calculations, tables, figure labels, and report narrative

No differential availability is detected between compared groups: the fraction of objects with unavailable width is tested per specimen and no group difference is found, with the confidence interval on the difference reported alongside the test so the detectable effect size is visible
known_limitations: Absolute nucleus diameter is not established. At 0.378 um per pixel against an approximately 0.23 um point spread function the image is about 3.3 times below Nyquist, and a deconvolved estimate saturates near 0.6 um, so PSF correction is disabled by default.
Response compresses below roughly one micron of true width, so a real difference in the thin regime appears reduced.

Integrated profile signal is far more sensitive to real width but scales directly with staining brightness. This study has no independent staining control, only same-genotype biological replicates, so integrated signal cannot separate a staining difference from a chromatin difference.

Profiles clipped at the instance boundary are dropped. On KJ-01 and WT-01 planes 34 to 36 this removed about 17 percent of detections, so the measured subset is not the full detection set and its group balance must be checked.

The measurement scopes profiles to the instance mask, so it still depends on segmentation for which pixels belong to the object, even though it does not depend on the mask boundary for the width value.

Criterion 10 requires that no differential availability is detected, not that the groups are equivalent. Two non-significant Welch tests cannot establish equivalence. On the 2026-09-14 cohort evidence the unavailable fraction differs by 0.90 percentage points with a 95 percent interval of -2.73 to +0.93, and the design detects roughly 2.5 percentage points at 80 percent power, so a smaller real imbalance would not have been found. Criterion 10 previously read 'does not differ materially', which has no defined margin and therefore could not be judged; the owner narrowed it on 2026-09-17 rather than declare a margin. Recorded in AGENT_CHANNEL.md [002] to [004].
non_claims: This is not a physical or PSF-corrected nucleus diameter.
Integrated profile signal is not a calibrated chromatin content measurement.
The signal-profile footprint proxy is not a filled-mask area and not an anatomical volume.
claims.notes: Supersedes MEAS-BODY-WIDTH-001 as the width presented biologically. Motivation: training annotations have a median width of 1.606 um against an optical nucleus width near 0.643 um, so the learned mask boundary is roughly 2.4 times too wide, and the bias is not constant across specimens. Measured on planes 34 to 36 after profile isolation was hardened, the mask to signal ratio was 2.12x on KJ-01 and 2.29x on WT-01, while the signal width difference between those specimens was 0.029 um against 0.115 um for the mask width. Not accepted: no independent audit run has been recorded against a clean commit. Availability bias was checked across all 35 specimens on three sampled planes each, 22381 detections. Width is unavailable for 21.4 percent of detections, dominated by boundary-clipped profiles at 76.9 percent of the unavailable set. The unavailable fraction does not differ between groups (KJ 0.2121, WT 0.2211, Welch p 0.325), and the selection bias does not differ either (KJ -0.540 um, WT -0.563 um, Welch p 0.305). The bias is negative in every one of the 35 specimens, meaning the dropped objects are narrower than the measured ones, so the measured subset skews wide by a similar amount in both groups. A shared and equal bias does not distort a between-group comparison, so the availability acceptance criterion is met on this evidence. DISCLOSURE FOR AUDIT: that run also produced a specimen-level signal-width group contrast, which was therefore seen before the audit gate passed. It is a technical readout on sampled planes without tracking, not a biological result, and no parameter, threshold or gate has been changed since it was seen.

claims.title: Slice-specific 3D ROI supports sampled SV volume
claims.statement: A reviewed Z-specific seminal-vesicle mask can support sampled SV volume and volume-normalized nucleus density; a repeated 2D ROI cannot.
claims.biological_meaning: The calibrated tissue volume actually represented by the reviewed slice-specific organ mask.
claims.population: all calibrated voxels inside the reviewed 3D SV mask
acceptance_criteria: Per-slice masks align with source planes
Volume is the calibrated sum of per-slice mask areas times Z spacing
Boundary truncation is reported
Repeated 2D ROI runs label anatomical volume unavailable
Count, volume, and density remain separate outcomes
known_limitations: Manual or interpolated organ boundaries require review
non_claims: A sampled or truncated mask is not necessarily complete anatomical SV volume

claims.title: Below-2-um tracks remain measurable with automated sensitivity analysis
claims.statement: Below-2-um technical-valid tracks remain in the primary biological population; an automated specimen-level sensitivity calculation reports how counts and summary morphometry would change if they were omitted, without creating a second accepted population or a routine manual-review queue.
claims.biological_meaning: Preserves genuine short nuclei and terminal optical sections while making potential fragment sensitivity transparent and reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: Primary technical-valid population is preserved
Short 2D observations remain eligible for morphology-neutral cross-slice linking
Specimen-level count and morphometry sensitivity is computed automatically
The sensitivity calculation is stored under technical QC and does not create a second user-facing biological population
known_limitations: Length alone cannot distinguish a genuine short nucleus from an unresolved fragment
non_claims: Length below 2 um is not automatically technical noise

claims.title: Routine biological reports expose one concise actionable result contract
claims.statement: Saturn v5.7.1 biological CSV, JSON, Excel, PDF, PowerPoint, and study-comparison outputs expose only the acquisition-coverage-sensitive estimated nucleus count, representative-section length, apparent central-body mask width, the same-plane length-to-width ratio, and representative-section centerline tortuosity; engineering and PSF-sensitive quantities remain in explicitly separated technical-QC artifacts.
claims.biological_meaning: A biologist has one unambiguous set of specimen outcomes and is not asked to choose among competing width, thickness, volume, density, or tracking diagnostics.
claims.population: technical-valid reconstructed nuclei summarized at specimen level
acceptance_criteria: Every routine biological surface contains the same five outcome definitions
Length and width used for the primary ratio come from the same representative plane
Primary tortuosity is measured from the centerline on that same representative plane; centroid track-path tortuosity remains technical QC

PSF-sensitive thickness, slab-volume proxies, repeated-2D-ROI density, P90, IQR, area-length width, legacy EDT width, pitch, taper, nearest-neighbor, and tracking diagnostics do not appear in biological PDF or PowerPoint artifacts
Detailed engineering outputs remain available under clearly named technical-QC paths
Between-group inference continues to use specimens rather than nuclei as independent replicates
known_limitations: Apparent body-mask width is not a PSF-corrected physical diameter
Estimated raw nucleus count depends on acquisition coverage until slice-specific anatomical ROI volume is implemented
non_claims: The concise report does not establish biological significance
The concise report does not measure anatomical seminal-vesicle volume

claims.title: GUI is the safe primary entry point for slice, batch, and study analysis
claims.statement: The Saturn v5.7.1 GUI uses one reviewed analysis path, blocks incomplete scientific inputs, preserves source data and prior attempts, reports progress and stop state truthfully, and prevents incomplete cohorts from producing biological group inference.
claims.biological_meaning: A biologist can run the same calibrated technical-valid analysis without command-line knowledge or silently changing the population, profile, checkpoint, specimen set, or comparison direction.
claims.population: GUI single-slice previews, full-stack batches, and multi-specimen studies
acceptance_criteria: Profile identity, checkpoint identity, calibration provenance, and scientific audit state are distinct visible readiness checks
Source and output directory trees never overlap
Stopped, failed, stale, or source-drifted attempts cannot be resumed or reported as complete
Every included specimen must be verified complete before biological group comparison
Reference and comparison roles control report direction without defining acceptable morphology
Overlay review is explicitly read-only until the append-only filled-mask correction workflow is independently accepted
known_limitations: Manual correction remains disabled until WORKFLOW-MANUAL-CORRECTION-001 is accepted
Long non-cancellable rendering stages must be labelled before they begin
non_claims: GUI readiness does not establish that every segmentation is biologically correct
A reference group is not a morphology target
